title: Addiction: Behaviour Change Models
welcome_lead: Theory of Planned Behaviour and Prochaska's stages — how change happens.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology addiction behaviour change theory of planned behaviour Prochaska stages.

Belief about social pressure to perform behaviour.

walkthroughs.body_html: Ajzen (1991) proposed three predictors of behavioural intention: attitude toward the behaviour, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control. Intention then predicts action. Meta-analyses (Armitage & Conner 2001) show TPB accounts for 27% of variance in behaviour.

Prochaska & DiClemente (1983) identified precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, maintenance, relapse. Interventions are most effective when matched to stage — motivational interviewing for contemplation, skills training for action.

NHS Stop Smoking services use TPB-based interventions: targeting beliefs about smoking, social norms and control. NRT doubles quit rates (Stead 2012). Stages of change underpin relapse prevention — relapse is normal and re-entry into the cycle.
